title: Universal relative lci parameter open between flat algebraic-space families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $A,C,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$ and $u:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ u=p$. Fibre products use [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is a local complete intersection morphism if on compatible etale scheme charts it locally factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with the ideal of the immersion locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]; the empty sequence is allowed. Assume that $p$ and $q$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, and that $|p|$ is closed, meaning it sends every closed subset of $|A|$ to a closed subset of $|B|$, in the point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. There exists an open subspace $W_{\mathrm{lci}}\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that for every algebraic space $B^\prime$ and morphism $g:B^\prime\to B$, the morphism $g$ factors through $W_{\mathrm{lci}}$ if and only if the induced map $u_{B^\prime}:A\times_BB^\prime\to C\times_BB^\prime$ is a local complete intersection morphism. In particular, when $B$ is a scheme, $W_{\mathrm{lci}}$ is an open subscheme of $B$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Neither $p$ nor $q$ is required to be surjective.

source.place: Tag 06CE (lemma-where-lci), statement; local complete intersection convention Tag 06C4 (definition-lci).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-lci-source-locus] to $A\xrightarrow{u}C\xrightarrow{q}B$ with $p=qu$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed flatness and local finite presentation of $p$ and $q$. Write $U=U(u)\subseteq A$ for the resulting open lci source locus. For every base change $g:B^\prime\to B$, the cited statement gives $U(u_{B^\prime})=A_{B^\prime}\times_AU$ and says that $u_{B^\prime}$ is lci exactly when this open is the whole source.

Set $D=|A|\setminus|U|$. It is closed because [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identifies the point set of an open subspace with an open subset. By the assumed closedness of $|p|$, $E=|p|(D)$ is closed in $|B|$. The open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives an open subspace $W_{\mathrm{lci}}\subseteq B$ with point set $|B|\setminus E$. Thus a base point belongs to this open exactly when it has no point of $D$ above it. This construction uses closedness only of $p$ itself.

source.place: Tag 06CE (lemma-where-lci), displayed definition of W and closedness argument; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $g:B^\prime\to B$. The fibre products $A^\prime=A\times_BB^\prime$ and $C^\prime=C\times_BB^\prime$ exist as algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Write $r:A^\prime\to A$ and $p^\prime:A^\prime\to B^\prime$ for their projections. Step 1 gives $U(u_{B^\prime})=A^\prime\times_AU$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], its point image is $|r|^{-1}(|U|)$; therefore its complement in $|A^\prime|$ is $D^\prime=|r|^{-1}(D)$.

source.place: Tag 06CE (lemma-where-lci), final base-change argument; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace).

proof.text: We claim $|p^\prime|(D^\prime)=|g|^{-1}(E)$. If $a^\prime\in D^\prime$, then $r(a^\prime)\in D$ and $g(p^\prime(a^\prime))=p(r(a^\prime))\in E$, giving one inclusion. Conversely, if $b^\prime\in |g|^{-1}(E)$, choose $a\in D$ with $p(a)=g(b^\prime)$. The surjectivity $|A\times_BB^\prime|\to|A|\times_{|B|}|B^\prime|$ in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] supplies $a^\prime$ above $(a,b^\prime)$. Then $a^\prime\in D^\prime$ and $p^\prime(a^\prime)=b^\prime$. This proves the claimed equality, and hence $D^\prime=\varnothing$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}|g|\subseteq|W_{\mathrm{lci}}|$.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), spelling out the set-theoretic inference in Tag 06CE.

proof.text: By step 1, $u_{B^\prime}$ is lci if and only if $U(u_{B^\prime})=A^\prime$. The full-point-image criterion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identifies this with $D^\prime=\varnothing$. By step 4 it is equivalent to $\operatorname{im}|g|\subseteq|W_{\mathrm{lci}}|$. The factorization assertion of [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] now gives the required factorization of $g$ through $W_{\mathrm{lci}}$; any such factorization conversely has that point-image containment. Finally, if $B$ is a scheme, the identity scheme test in [def-a1-space-open-subspace] identifies $W_{\mathrm{lci}}=B\times_BW_{\mathrm{lci}}$ with an open subscheme of $B$. No step required either family to be surjective.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q07-1abfcc118 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full against spaces-more-morphisms.tex 06C4 definition-lci, 06CA lemma-base-change-lci-fibres and 06CE lemma-where-lci. The item statement matches 06CE exactly: p and q flat and locally of finite presentation, only |p| closed, arbitrary algebraic-space base change, no surjectivity, and the scheme clause comes from def-a1-space-open-subspace. Steps 2 to 5 follow the proof of 06CE and the cited statements give each use: point-open-calculus (D closed, 03H4 point lifting, full-image criterion), etale-open-image (W), open-factor-scheme-tests (arbitrary pullback point image, factorization) and fibre-products. The new node lem-sfb-space-relative-lci-source-locus is the relative 06CA. It is not a duplicate: the fibrewise-lci-source-locus, lci-base-open and scheme-lci-etale-locality nodes state different things. It is not a restatement of the item (D1). I tested it on an empty A, on u = identity of a singular flat family, and on Spec k -> A^1_k cut out by x. FIX: step 1 says the node shows u_{B'} is lci exactly when the open is the whole source, but the node stated this only for u (C4). I appended to the node's statement that u' is lci iff A' x_A U(u) = A'; this follows directly from source-locality in 06C4.
